data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 1-of-9 loss is not a property of the test at all but of the mutation's blast radius: the mutation was lost because no test in the same repository imports the mutated module under the shown-to-fail-first installation, so the distribution 3-of-26 vs 1-of-9 is an artifact of import graph topology, not of description versus constraint.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the lost mutation's module did have a test importer but the test was skipped under shown-to-fail-first, the topology claim is incomplete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the import graph saturation is uniform across modules, the observed distribution cannot be explained by topology.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 result includes mutations with saturated import graphs that still survived, the topology claim is insufficient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A test constrains a subject if and only if the test's import graph reaches the subject's mutated code path. The 1/9 mutation was in a module with no test importer under the installation order, while the ordinarily-guarded modules had 4/4 to 6/7 because their import graphs were saturated. The asymmetry is a confound: one repository, one author, one week, and the mutations were proposed by models that had read the acceptance record.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
